summary: Backend HTTP tests for the hr_scope unit-isolation feature (letters, fee stats, management dashboard, activity logs), using temporary custom users U1 (scope: Girls faculty) and U2 (scope: Sharia faculty). 12 of 16 tests in the new file pass. Passing: general-letter isolation (issue, list, GET 403, revoke 403, draft stamping), activity-logs isolation, and the dean/department_head/admin regression (Salim still sees 20 students, his letter set and dashboard numbers are unchanged; Saeed is unchanged). Failing (4): a custom user with only hr_scope=UNITS and no academic faculty/department assignment gets 0 students in /fees/stats and /fees/unpaid-students, and an empty department list in /dashboard/management. The expected result was 72 students. Isolation only narrows correctly when the user already has an academic scope: a variant user with faculty_ids=[Girls, Sharia] went from 92 to 72 students. All test users, letters, drafts and series counters were cleaned up.

critical.issue: A custom user with hr_scope=UNITS on Girls faculty and no faculty_id/department_ids gets total_students=0 and departments=[] (expected 72 and [الدراسات الإسلامية]). Cause: get_user_scope_filter returns the fail-safe impossible filter {_id: ObjectId('000..0')} for role 'custom' with no academic data (server.py ~L1290-1298). _apply_hr_scope then ANDs it with the hr_scope departments, so the result is always empty. The 5 new HR users (HR manager, finance manager, services manager, secretary, employee) will typically have hr_scope only, so they will see no students at all.
Same cause: for U1 and U2, scope.departments=[] and faculties=[], so the dashboard is empty instead of showing only their own faculty.

minor.issue: General-letter isolation only applies when the user has HR_PERMS (hr_manage_correspondence/hr_manage_employees). A custom user with only issue_letters (e.g. the director's secretary) and hr_scope=Sharia gets 200 on a general letter issued from Girls scope (verified via HTTP). The user's decision #4 covers holders of HR or official-letter permissions, so the gate should probably also include issue_letters.
No scope filtering. A restricted custom user with view_activity_logs gets university-wide by_action/by_user/by_day totals. The user asked to isolate the activity log.

The deleted-items bin is not isolated by hr_scope, although the user included it in scope (سجل النشاط والمحذوفات). It returns all items to any holder of manage_courses/manage_students/manage_teachers.

The isolation branch only applies to role=='custom'. Other non-academic roles (employee, registrar, registration_manager) with view_activity_logs and a restricted hr_scope are not isolated, while fees and dashboard isolate every non-academic role. The coverage rules are inconsistent between modules.

action_items: Fix _apply_hr_scope (fee_receipts.py) and _resolve_scope (management_dashboard.py): when the academic base filter is the fail-safe {_id: ObjectId('000000000000000000000000')} (or {}) and hr_scope_isolation_department_ids returns a non-empty list, use the hr_scope departments alone as the scope. Re-run test_unit_isolation_hr_scope.py; expect U1 to see 72 students and only the Girls dept on the dashboard.
Decide whether issue_letters-only users with a restricted hr_scope should be isolated in letters._visible_filter (currently gated on HR_PERMS only).
Add hr_scope isolation to GET /api/activity-logs/stats and GET /api/trash, as the user requested (activity log + deleted items).
Align which roles are isolated: activity-logs covers only 'custom', while fees and dashboard cover every non-academic role.
critical_code_review_comments: The isolation helpers only intersect with the existing academic scope and never grant a scope. A user configured only through the HR scope screen therefore sees nothing in fees and the dashboard, which defeats the feature for the intended HR users.

created_by_faculty_ids is stamped in _finalize_fields for every issuer (empty list for unrestricted users). Letters issued before this change have no stamp and stay visible to everyone by design, which is acceptable.
Issued letters cannot be deleted through the API (drafts only), and issuing a test letter consumes a series serial. The tests restore letter_series counters directly in Mongo during cleanup.

Older test scripts call sys.exit()/asyncio.run at import (test_hr_scope_stage_b.py, test_absence_excuses_app.py, test_letters_drafts.py, etc.), which crashes the collection run 'pytest backend/tests -k ...' with INTERNALERROR. Convert them to pytest or rename them so they are not collected.

rca of the issue: Repro: create a role=custom user with manage_fee_receipts and no faculty_id/department_ids, set PUT /api/hr/users/{id}/scope {hr_scope:'UNITS', hr_scope_unit_ids:['6ab3ec870186d4c5e32749a6']}, then call GET /api/fees/stats: total_students=0. Root cause: server.get_user_scope_filter returns {_id: ObjectId('0'*24)} as a fail-safe for scoped roles with no academic data. fee_receipts._apply_hr_scope and management_dashboard._resolve_scope build {$and: [base, {department_id/_id: {$in: hr_depts}}]}, so the impossible base empties the result. Proof: the same user with faculty_ids=[Girls, Sharia] correctly drops from 92 to 72. Mitigation: treat the fail-safe/empty base as 'no academic scope' when an hr_scope isolation list exists, and use only the hr_scope list.
